description: Generates hybrid personalized recommendations combining behavior, resources, and performance

low_performance_low_hours.message: Your study hours and performance are both below target. Let's build a foundation.
actions: Start with 30-minute daily study sessions and gradually increase
Focus on one subject at a time — avoid multitasking
Use Active Recall to make the most of limited study time
Set 3 small achievable goals each day
Visit office hours or ask peers for help on difficult topics

low_performance_high_hours.message: You're putting in the hours but results aren't matching your effort. Let's improve your study efficiency.
actions: Switch from passive reading to Active Recall and self-testing
Try the Feynman Technique to identify gaps in understanding
Take regular breaks — use Pomodoro Technique (25/5 pattern)
Review your notes within 24 hours of each lecture
Focus on understanding concepts rather than memorizing

high_performance_low_hours.message: You're performing well with minimal study time. Great efficiency! But there's room to grow.
actions: Challenge yourself with advanced problems or bonus assignments
Help peers through study groups — teaching deepens understanding
Explore supplementary resources beyond the syllabus
Consider research projects or extra-curricular academic activities
Build a portfolio of projects related to your courses

high_performance_high_hours.message: Excellent work! You're dedicated and achieving results. Focus on maintaining balance.
actions: Monitor for burnout — ensure you have rest days
Mentor other students in study groups
Explore research or internship opportunities
Set long-term academic goals beyond this semester
Diversify your study techniques to stay engaged

inconsistent_pattern.message: Your study pattern is inconsistent. Building a routine will significantly improve your results.
actions: Set a fixed daily study time and treat it like a class
Use Time Blocking to allocate specific hours to each subject
Track your study sessions daily — accountability helps consistency
Start small: 2 consistent hours are better than 6 inconsistent ones
Remove distractions during study blocks — use app blockers if needed

deadline_approaching.message: You have upcoming deadlines. Let's prioritize your tasks.
actions: List all tasks due this week and sort by deadline
Focus on high-priority tasks first
Break large tasks into smaller subtasks
Allocate focused 2-hour blocks for each major task
Ask for extensions early if you're overwhelmed — professors appreciate honesty

exam_preparation: Start reviewing at least 7 days before the exam
Create summary sheets for each chapter
Practice with past exams and sample questions
Use spaced repetition for key definitions and formulas
Get adequate sleep — at least 7 hours before exam day
assignment_completion: Read the entire assignment brief before starting
Break the assignment into milestones with mini-deadlines
Start with the hardest part when your energy is highest
Use a checklist to ensure all requirements are met
project_management: Define clear roles and responsibilities for team projects
Use version control for code projects
Document your work as you go — don't leave it for the end
Plan for buffer time — unexpected issues always arise

motivation_tips: Remember your WHY — why did you choose this field?
Celebrate small wins — every completed task is progress
Visualize your future self graduating and succeeding
Connect with motivated peers who push you forward
Track your progress — seeing improvement is motivating
Take care of your health — exercise, eat well, sleep enough
When feeling stuck, switch to a different subject or take a walk
Set rewards for completing difficult tasks
